costGuide.title: Mercedes-Benz OM612 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an OM612 engine typically takes 10-14 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.
paragraphs: What genuinely moves the price for this engine is the condition of the swirl flap system, injector seals, and turbocharger actuator. Because the OM612 is an early common-rail design, recon specialists often upgrade the swirl flap mechanism to a more reliable aftermarket unit or perform a verified delete, alongside replacing all injector seals as standard. failures.title: Mercedes-Benz OM612 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Swirl Flap Motor Failure - All variants
items.whatHappens: The plastic gears inside the electronic swirl flap motor strip over time, causing the ECU to throw a check engine light and default the engine to limp mode. In some cases, the flaps themselves can seize in the inlet manifold due to carbon buildup.
items.repairVsReplace: The actuator motor can be replaced independently and relatively cheaply. However, if the flaps are seized or the manifold is heavily carboned, a full inlet manifold replacement or verified delete is required.

items.title: Injector Seal Weeping ("Black Death") - All variants
items.whatHappens: The copper washer seals at the base of the injectors degrade, allowing high-pressure combustion gases to escape. This creates a black, crusty carbon buildup around the injector heads, leading to a distinct tapping noise, rough idling, and a strong smell of exhaust in the cabin.
items.repairVsReplace: This is a routine maintenance item, not a terminal failure. Replacing the seals and cleaning the cylinder head is inexpensive and should be done preventatively.

items.title: Turbocharger Actuator Wear - High-mileage units
items.whatHappens: The wastegate actuator rod and linkage can corrode or seize, leading to inconsistent boost pressure, sluggish acceleration, and potential over-boosting if the flap sticks closed.
items.repairVsReplace: Actuator replacement is a straightforward and cost-effective repair. If the turbocharger internals have suffered damage from prolonged over-boosting, a full turbo rebuild or replacement is necessary.

failures.goodYearsLine: The OM612 is generally more robust than the 4-cylinder OM611 it succeeded, featuring a stronger block and fewer timing chain issues. Units maintained with regular oil changes and timely injector seal replacements routinely exceed 250,000 miles without major internal issues .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the Mercedes-Benz OM612
variants.intro: ═══════════════════════════════════════ The engine code is stamped on the right-hand side of the cylinder block, just above the oil filter housing. It will also be listed on your V5C logbook under "Engine Capacity" or visible via a VIN decode. The OM612 is sometimes confused with the 4-cylinder OM611 or the V6 OM642. Fitting the wrong revision or assuming interchangeability matters significantly: the OM612 has a unique 5-cylinder firing order, specific engine mounts, and a distinct wiring loom and ECU mapping that will not function correctly in a 4- or 6-cylinder chassis.

relatives.description: the 2.5L inline-5 pre-chamber diesel that the OM612 replaced, sharing the same smooth 5-cylinder firing order but lacking the efficiency and torque of the common-rail architecture.
the 3.0L V6 CDI that largely took over the mid-range torque role in later E-Class and M-Class models, offering higher outputs but with a more complex V-layout and different failure profile.
the smaller 2.1L/2.2L 4-cylinder CDI that sits directly below the OM612 in the hierarchy, sharing the same electronic injection principles but with less low-end pulling power.
the later 2.1L/2.2L 4-cylinder CDI that replaced the OM611, often confused with the OM612 due to overlapping production years in the W211 E-Class, though it is physically a different block.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement OM612 Engine - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used OM612 engine makes sense only if it comes with verifiable service history and documented replacement of the swirl flap actuator and injector seals. Given the age of these vehicles, the primary risk is hidden carbon buildup or degraded rubber components, so a compression test is mandatory before purchase.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned OM612 engine is the sweet spot for most buyers. A reputable rebuild will address the common failure points by upgrading or replacing the swirl flap system, fitting new injector seals, and refreshing the turbo actuator, giving the engine a fresh lease on life.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full OM612 engine rebuild is justified for high-mileage G-Class applications or classic W211 E-Class restorations where originality and maximum longevity are required. An upgraded rebuild should include line-boring the block, new pistons/rings, and a balanced crankshaft.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting through our vetted network ensures your OM612 engine is installed by specialists familiar with early Mercedes CDI systems, backed by a nationwide warranty.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Because the OM612 is typically found in W203, W210, W211, W163, and W463 vehicles valued between £2,000 and £8,000, a full replacement can represent a significant portion of the host's worth. If the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value before committing .

items.question: What is the most common failure on the OM612 engine?
items.answer: The most documented issues are swirl flap motor failure, injector seal weeping ("Black Death"), and turbocharger actuator wear. Swirl flap motor failure triggers limp mode and is a routine fix, whereas injector seal failure causes black carbon buildup and rough idling but is a cheap and preventative maintenance item. → Get quotes for a rebuilt OM612 with these issues resolved

items.question: Which Mercedes models use the OM612 engine?
items.answer: The OM612 was fitted to the W203 C-Class (C 270 CDI), the W210 and W211 E-Class (E 270 CDI), the W163 M-Class (ML 270 CDI), and the W463 G-Class (G 270 CDI), serving as the definitive 5-cylinder diesel for these chassis between 2000 and 2005. → Check your registration to confirm your exact OM612 fitment

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned OM612 engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned OM612 is strongly recommended over a used unit. A proper rebuild will proactively address the common failure points by upgrading or replacing the swirl flap system, fitting new injector seals, and refreshing the turbo actuator, whereas used engines often hide stretched components and carboned manifolds. → Compare reconditioned OM612 engine prices from UK specialists

items.answer: The OM612 is a distinct 2.7L inline-5, producing a unique 5-cylinder rumble compared to the 4-cylinder OM611 or the V6 OM642.
